beats.text: A function of two inputs can change in more than one direction. A partial derivative asks what happens when one input moves while the other stays fixed. On this bowl, each coordinate direction gives its own local slope.

Fix y equal to one and move only x. The cross-section becomes x squared plus one, so its slope is two x. At x equal to one, the partial slope is two; the frozen y contribution behaves like a constant.

At the point one, negative one, increasing x initially raises the surface, while increasing y initially lowers it. The two partial derivatives are two and negative two. A single height does not determine how the surface tilts in every direction.

beats.formula: x=t, y=2t: quad frac(dif f,dif t)=10t
beats.text: If both coordinates move along a path, neither partial derivative alone is the full rate. Along x equals t and y equals two t, the height is five t squared. Its derivative is ten t, combining both coordinate contributions.

practice.prompt: For f(x,y)=3x²+2y², find both partial derivatives at (2,−1). Explain which variable stays fixed in each calculation.
practice.answer: f_x=6x, so f_x(2,−1)=12; f_y=4y, so f_y(2,−1)=−4. Hold y fixed for f_x and x fixed for f_y.

practice.prompt: For g(x,y)=x²y³, find g_x and g_y, then evaluate both at (1,2).
practice.answer: g_x=2xy³ and g_y=3x²y². At (1,2), they are 16 and 12 respectively.

practice.prompt: Let f=x²+y² and follow x=t, y=3t. Find df/dt at t=2 and explain why using only f_x would be incomplete.
practice.answer: Along the path f=10t², so df/dt=20t=40 at t=2. Both x and y change; equivalently f_x x′+f_y y′=2t+18t.

takeaway: A partial derivative freezes the other inputs; rates along a path must account for every moving coordinate.
scope: Coordinate slices and the distinction between partial and total change along a path.
title: Partial derivatives
objective: Distinguish coordinate rates, directional derivatives, gradients, and differentiability.
